prompt: You know one acute angle of a right triangle and the length of the hypotenuse, and you want the leg **adjacent** to that angle. Which ratio should you use?

choices.label: The Pythagorean theorem — trigonometry cannot help here

hint: List the two sides in play: the one you want (adjacent) and the one you know (hypotenuse).

hints.text: List the two sides in play: the one you want (adjacent) and the one you know (hypotenuse).
Which of the three ratios connects exactly adjacent and hypotenuse?

explanation: Pick the ratio by which two sides are involved, never by habit.
Adjacent plus hypotenuse is the cosine pair (CAH).
Tangent needs the opposite side, which you do not know, and the Pythagorean theorem needs two sides, not an angle. Choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: A two-second routine
steps: Mark the angle, then label the three sides: opposite, adjacent, hypotenuse.
Circle the side you know and the side you want; the two circles pick the ratio for you every single time.
